newsitem.title: USA: Payless ShoeSource to buy J. Baker unit.
newsitem.headline: Payless ShoeSource to buy J. Baker unit.

text.p: Payless ShoeSource Inc and J. Baker Inc said Tuesday they had signed a definitive agreement for Payless to buy J. Baker's Parade of Shoes division.
Parade of Shoes had sales of $113 million in 1995.

Payless will purchase the Parade of Shoes stores, inventory and trademarks. The sale, scheduled to be completed in early 1997, is subject to transfer of leases on Parade of Shoes stores and the expiration or termination of the waiting period under federal antitrust law.
Parade of Shoes sells women's footwear and accessories in 186 stores in 14 states.
Parade offers primarily leather private-label footwear, priced from $20 to $40 a pair, in self-service stores. Major markets include Boston, New York, Chicago, Philadelphia and Washington.
Payless said it plans to operate Parade of Shoes as a separate division.

"We intend to maintain a distinct positioning for Parade of Shoes, serving different customer needs at higher price points than the footwear we sell through Payless ShoeSource stores," Steven Douglass, chairman, said in a statement.
Payless said it intends to interview current Parade of Shoes sales associates for potential positions under Payless ownership.
Commenting an the transaction, Alan Weinstein, J. Baker president, said the acquisition of Parade of Shoes by Payless will continue the expansion of this retail concept.
"Although we believe in this niche business, the concept no longer fits into J. Baker's long-term strategy," Weinstein said.

J. Baker operates 1,014 licensed footwear departments in discount department stores, 459 licensed footwear departments in semi-service and full-service department and specialty apparel stores, 186 Parade of Shoes stores, 442 Casual Male Big & Tall stores, and 66 Work 'N Gear stores.
Payless is a footwear retailer with 4,261 stores.
